title: $\RHom$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be one of $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite;
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) or $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), and let $X$
be a scheme of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K,L\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ are bounded
constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(K,L)$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]).

external.place: Since $K$ is bounded constructible, reduction modulo $\varpi$ gives $$ \RHom(K,L)/\varpi\cong\RHom_{\cO_E/\varpi}(K/\varpi,L/\varpi). $$ By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal $\RHom$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.6) on the finite type $k$-scheme $X$, with coefficients in which $p$ is invertible, this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: First consider $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$. The only ideals of $k$ are $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Choose a uniformizer $t$ of $A_0=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A=A_0/(t)$ is a finite field; its characteristic is $\ell$, since $\ell$ belongs to the maximal ideal. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], the actual coefficient ring is $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_0/t^n)_X$. The bounded-constructible hypothesis on $K$ and $L$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] means bounded cohomology constructible by general local finite presentations. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] to each cohomology sheaf of $K$ and $L$: both complexes have bounded cohomology with finite constant local models. This invocation is the coefficient-specific bridge, not an identification by definition. Now apply implication (1) to (2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion], whose condition (1) explicitly uses finite constant scalar models. It gives local derived $(t)$-completeness of $K,L$, in the sense used by that criterion, and identifies $K_1=K\otimes_B^LA_X$, $L_1=L\otimes_B^LA_X$ with bounded finite-Tor-amplitude étale complexes with constructible finite-dimensional $A$-cohomology. Hence these reductions satisfy the explicit finite constant local model hypotheses of the finite-field child below.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); Stacks Tag 09C0, proetale.tex, section-suitable-derived, for the adic criterion. The general-lfp to scalar-model comparison is the separate agent obligation cited in this step.

proof.text:
Set $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] to this $B$ and $n=1$, with its finite-field datum taken in the characteristic $p$ of $k$, so that its hypothesis $\ell\ne p$ is the one in force. Its statement applies to an arbitrary scheme and arbitrary ambient complexes; it does not impose a finite-ground-field or site-perfectness hypothesis. Its evaluation-defined comparison gives
$$H\otimes_B^LA_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K_1,L_1).$$
This is a comparison of the ambient internal Homs, not a new choice of Hom on a constructible subcategory. The completeness clause of that lemma is not used here: it concerns the derived-limit notion of completeness of its own definitions, whereas the criterion of step 1 uses local derived completeness; step 3 proves the latter for $H$ directly.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-internal-hom-finiteness] to the finite field $A$ and to $K_1,L_1$ with their scalar-constant constructible cohomology established in step 1. By step 2, $H\otimes_B^LA_X$ is therefore bounded with finite constant local model cohomology. Apply [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] on the Noetherian (hence qcqs) scheme $X$, with the discrete Noetherian field $A$, to obtain a bounded constructible étale complex $C$ whose pullback is this reduction. It has finite Tor amplitude: tensor of $A$-module sheaves is exact, as is checked locally by tensor of vector spaces and exact sheafification; consequently for a bounded complex its derived tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has the same cohomological support bound. Next, $H$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, let $f\in(t)(U)$, and write $B_U$ for the restricted ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and on the slice site over $U$, together with the symmetry of the derived tensor product,
$$\begin{aligned}
R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],H|_U)&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U,L|_U))\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_U}B_U[1/f],L|_U)\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U,R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],L|_U))=0,
\end{aligned}$$
the last vanishing being the local derived completeness of $L$ from step 1. Together with this completeness of $H$, the étale complex $C$ verifies condition (2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion]. Its implication (2) to (1) gives bounded cohomology of $H$ with finite constant scalar local models. The reverse direction of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] makes these cohomology sheaves constructible in the general ring-object sense. Thus $H$ meets exactly the bounded-constructible predicate in the conclusion [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 with R=A and m=0; Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); Stacks Tag 09AI, proetale.tex, constructible comparison, and Tag 09C0, section-suitable-derived. Completeness of internal Hom: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.13 proof (adjunction), via the ringed-site tensor–Hom adjunction and slice restriction.

proof.text:
All calculations use the ordinary unbounded layer-B category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\operatorname{Ab}),B))$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The bounded-constructible predicate used for $K,L$ and the conclusion [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] is the general stratified local-finite-presentation predicate [def-sfb-constructible-module], allowing arbitrary coefficient-sheaf matrix entries. It does not by definition impose the scalar-constant predicate [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For integral coefficients these predicates agree on this Noetherian $X$ by [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison]. For $\underline E$ and $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, apply respectively [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] and [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality] to each Noetherian locally closed stratum of each general-lfp cohomology sheaf. Their coefficient rings are the item's rings: the inverse image $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}\circ a^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] is, term by term, the sheafified left Kan extension along $S\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$ followed by inverse image along $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, which is the definition of $p_T^*$ in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]; and the condensed rings $C(-,E)$ and $\underline\Omega$ used there are $\underline E$ and $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ by their sections. So $E^c_T=E_T$, and the ring $p_T^*\underline\Omega$ of the second lemma is $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,T}$, as ring sheaves, and their cokernel presentations are those of [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. The resulting locally finite free modules are finite constant local models, with scalar model $E^r$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^r$. Conversely a scalar-constant finite-presentation matrix is an allowed coefficient-sheaf finite-presentation matrix, since extension of scalars preserves its cokernel. Thus scalar-constant constructible cohomology implies general-lfp constructible cohomology for each ring. Boundedness is the same cohomological condition throughout. These are coefficient-specific comparison arguments, separate from the ambient category identification. We record the formal change-of-ring identification used in the remaining comparisons. For a coefficient-ring map $R\to S$, write $T_S=S\otimes_R^LT$ and $U$ for restriction. The derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], strong tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the identity topos with ring map $R\to S$, and tensor-Hom adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] give, for every test object $T$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,U R\mathcal Hom_S(K_S,N))
&=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T_S\otimes_S^LK_S,N)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_S((T\otimes_R^LK)_S,N)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,R\mathcal Hom_R(K,UN)).
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality in $T$ identifies $U R\mathcal Hom_S(K_S,N)$ with $R\mathcal Hom_R(K,UN)$. The identification carries evaluation to the scalar-extended evaluation, since all three displayed bijections are the indicated adjunction bijections. Restriction is conservative: it leaves the underlying complexes of abelian sheaves unchanged.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.10, Remark 6.8.15; separate coefficient-specific lfp comparison inputs are cited explicitly. The displayed change-of-ring calculation is formal from the three cited adjunction/tensor statements.

proof.text:
For integral $K_0,L_0$ bounded constructible in the general-lfp sense, [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] applied to the cohomology of $K_0$ supplies the finite constant local models required by [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity]. This also applies to the integral representatives later furnished by the rationalization equivalence; no stronger hypothesis on those representatives is assumed. Take a bounded-below complex representative of $L_0$. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $E_X=B[1/\ell]$ is the sequential colimit in sheaves of $B$-modules, equipped with its localization ring structure. Tensoring this module colimit with the representative gives the termwise colimit of $L_0\xrightarrow{\ell}L_0\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$. This system has a common lower bound. By [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity],
$$R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)[1/\ell]
\simeq R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0[1/\ell]).$$
Here the left side is the same scalar localization of internal Hom. The module-object category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], so filtered colimits are exact; tensoring with $B[1/\ell]$ is therefore exact, being the filtered colimit of tensoring with the free module $B$. Step 4 identifies the right side with the restriction of $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}((K_0)_E,(L_0)_E)$. Hence the canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$E_X\otimes_B^L R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}((K_0)_E,(L_0)_E)$$
is an isomorphism. Indeed its restriction is precisely the continuity map above; scalar multiplication by $\ell$ on the target is invertible, so the compatible maps from the stages define the displayed localized map.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); internal continuity is the explicitly named additional input.

proof.text: For arbitrary bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K,L$, apply [def-sfb-rationalization-equivalence] with the fixed prime $\ell$, finite subextension $E$ and its pulled-back coefficient rings. Its composite with localization is the restriction of $E_X\otimes_B^L-$ to bounded constructible complexes. The equivalence therefore gives integral bounded constructible representatives $K_0,L_0$ with $(K_0)_E\simeq K$ and $(L_0)_E\simeq L$: the standard localization has the objects of its source, and the equivalence is compatible with scalar extension. These representatives initially satisfy only the general-lfp predicate; step 5 applies to them because it explicitly invokes the integral comparison lemma. Step 3 makes $H_0=R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)$ bounded constructible. By [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-bounded-constructible], $(H_0)_E$ is bounded constructible. The evaluation-compatible comparison proved in step 5 identifies it with $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K,L)$. This proves the rational finite-extension case.

For bounded constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$-complexes $K,L$, choose a common finite field $E$ and bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K_E,L_E$ representing both, by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. To obtain a common field from two initial fields, take their compositum and apply [lem-sfb-extend-subfield-constructible]. Put $H_E=R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,L_E)$, bounded constructible by step 6. For every finite $F/E$, [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] identifies $F_X$ with a finite sum of $E_X$. Thus, after restriction, the canonical map
$$F_X\otimes_{E_X}^LH_E\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{F_X}((K_E)_F,(L_E)_F)$$
is the finite-sum identification $H_E^{[F:E]}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,L_E^{[F:E]})$, using step 4. Its action on each basis summand is the identity followed by multiplication by that basis element. A different basis or the inclusion $F\subset F'$ gives a finite matrix of $E$-scalars; additivity and $E$-linearity of internal Hom make the same matrix act on both sides. Hence these are the evaluation-defined comparisons and commute with every field transition map, not just abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1)–(2) and Remark 6.8.15; finite-free scalar calculation.

proof.text:
Use the filtered coefficient-ring colimit of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Restricting its index to finite subfields $F$ containing the chosen $E$ leaves the same colimit: each finite subfield $F_0$ maps to the finite compositum $EF_0$, and any two such choices map to their compositum. Thus $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}=\varinjlim_{F\supset E}F_X$. A bounded-below representative of $L_E$ gives a diagram $F_X\otimes_{E_X}L_E$ with the same termwise lower bound, because these coefficient modules are finite free. The module-object category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], so the filtered colimit of these exact finite-free tensor functors is exact and represents derived extension to the colimit coefficient ring. The descended $K_E$ from step 7 initially has only general-lfp constructible cohomology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] on each Noetherian stratum of each cohomology sheaf to make it pro-étale locally finite free. It therefore has precisely the finite constant local models required to apply [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity] with rational coefficients. Together with the compatible finite-sum maps in step 7 and the adjunction calculation in step 4 this identifies, after restriction to $E_X$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}^LH_E
&\simeq\varinjlim_F(F_X\otimes_{E_X}H_E)\\
&\simeq\varinjlim_F R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,F_X\otimes_{E_X}L_E)\\
&\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}L_E)\\
&\simeq U R\mathcal Hom_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}}(K,L).
\end{aligned}$$
The comparison is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation and is therefore $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$-linear. Restriction is conservative, so it is an isomorphism in the target coefficient category. Finally [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible] makes the scalar extension of $H_E$ bounded constructible. Thus the target internal Hom is bounded constructible, proving the last case.

split_report.blueprint: The current main-20261015 proof of lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves (lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves.proof.md) is one paragraph. Its first sentence, 'use the characterisation of bounded constructible complexes recalled in the proof of [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]', is realized by step 1 (general-lfp to scalar models by the integral comparison, then the integral adic criterion). 'The complex RHom(K,L) is derived varpi-complete, since L is' is realized in step 3 by the local derived completeness argument; 'reduction modulo varpi gives RHom(K,L)/varpi = RHom(K/varpi,L/varpi)' is step 2. 'By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal RHom (SGA 4 1/2, Th. finitude 1.6) ... this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology' is step 3 through the finite-field child, sourced to Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.7.13 instead of SGA 4 1/2 under the no-SGA route lock, followed by the converse adic criterion. 'The cases E and Qlbar follow by inverting ell' is steps 4-6 (scalar adjunction, internal continuity under localization, rationalization equivalence); 'and by descending to a finite extension E ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]) ... see Bhatt-Scholze 6.8' is steps 7-8.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q36-aefdb3068 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the blueprint statement and its existing proof file (lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves.proof.md), the unit, every cited node statement, and Bhatt–Scholze 6.3.13/6.3.14/6.3.16/6.5.1/6.7.11/6.7.13/6.8.10–6.8.15 plus the HRS references. The item statement equals the blueprint text, with nothing weakened and the general-lfp predicate kept. All three new nodes are true, self-contained, not duplicates and not restatements. (a) The finite-field Hom finiteness is BS 6.7.13 with R=A, m=0, using Gabber finiteness and no SGA. (b) Internal continuity is the internal form of BS 6.3.14/6.8.12 and keeps the common lower bound. (c) I checked the integral lfp ⇔ scalar-model comparison independently: sections over w-contractible covers are constant on connected components, which are strictly henselian, so fibre types are constant along specialization and Smith form holds continuously; torsion and geometric-point cases pass. Three repairable faults are fixed in fixes/. Fault 1 (C4/E6): steps 2–3 mixed def-weil-derived-complete (the completeness clause of lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction) with the locally derived completeness of the adic criterion, and nothing connected the two. Step 3 now proves local derived completeness of H directly via lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction; that tool use is declared, and step 2 notes the datum p=char k. Fault 2 (E6): step 4 used the E/Q̄ℓ lfp local-triviality lemmas, stated for the coefficient sheaves of def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, without saying they are the item's Λ_X. The identification is now stated and cited. Fault 3 (B9): split_report.blueprint and the three from.place fields claimed the blueprint item has no proof text, but the proof exists. They now name its sentences: characterisation → step 1; reduction mod ϖ → step 2; completeness and Deligne finiteness → step 3, sourced to BS 6.7.13 under the no-SGA lock; inverting ℓ → steps 4–6; descent to E → steps 7–8. proof_deps was recomputed and all cited ids exist.
